verdict: A quiet day: one real tool release (mGear 5.4), a few VFX breakdowns worth a glance, and a lot of SEO listicle noise and unrelated ML papers that don't belong in this digest.

stories.headline: mGear 5.4, free open-source Maya rigging toolset, adds unified facial rigging
stories.body: mGear 5.4 is out with unified facial rigging, a redesigned Anim Picker, and 3D onion skinning added to the open-source rigging framework for Maya. It remains free and open source, making it one of the few actively maintained community rigging toolsets usable directly on client work without licence concerns.
stories.why: Free rigging toolset update is directly deployable in a Maya pipeline today.

stories.headline: Chaos publishes framework for using AI rendering in studio client pitches
stories.body: Chaos published an operational guide aimed at studio leads on where AI-generated visuals fit in architecture/vis pitch workflows, covering ownership and governance failures that can damage client trust. It's a process piece, not a tool release, but relevant for studios already using AI rendering in early-stage client communication.
stories.why: Addresses governance risk for studios already slipping AI renders into client pitches.

stories.headline: Hungry: Magic Dust VFX breakdown shows CG hippo creature and water sim work on limited budget
stories.body: UK studio Magic Dust VFX published a breakdown of its creature and water simulation work for the feature Hungry, detailing how it built and animated a CG hippopotamus with constrained resources. Useful as a case study in doing complex creature/fluid FX on a smaller-budget show rather than a big-tentpole pipeline.
stories.why: Concrete small-studio creature/fluid FX case study, relevant to boutique-scale production.

stories.headline: This Hack Fixes Your AI Character Consistency Issues (Pro Workflow)
stories.body: A comparison between 'headless' character sheets and robust multiview sheets for maintaining identity in AI video.
stories.why: Integrates into pre-viz or rapid prototyping stages for generative asset creation before formal hand-authoring.

stories.headline: You Can Now Create Modular 3D Character Without Blender
stories.body: The release of AI-driven modular character decomposition, allowing a single reference image to be split into discrete, animatable 3D parts automatically.
stories.why: Useful for rapid pre-vis asset generation. Current lack of direct USD support limits it to FBX/GLB workflows. Reconciling AI-generated UVs and intersections still requires manual cleanup in Blender/ZBrush.
